newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SINGAPORE MAS TO ATTEND IMF MEETING ON THAILAND.
newsitem.headline: SINGAPORE MAS TO ATTEND IMF MEETING ON THAILAND.

text.p: Singapore's de facto central bank said on Friday it would attend a meeting organised by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) to discuss a rescue package for Thailand in Tokyo on Monday.
"The MAS (Monetary Authority of Singapore) will be represented at the IMF-organised meeting in Tokyo to discuss the IMF financial plan for Thailand," an MAS spokesman told Reuters.
He did not comment on how much, if any, aid Singapore would extend to Thailand.
The IMF said on Thursday it would convene a meeting of interested countries and institutions on August 11 in Tokyo to discuss a financing package for Thailand's ailing economy.

In addition to Japan and the IMF, officials from the Asian Development Bank and the World Bank are expected to attend the meeting along with representatives of China, Hong Kong, Australia and the United States.
No details of the size of the package have been confirmed, but Thailand has said it was seeking $12 to $15 billion in international loans.
The MAS spokesman said the central bank did not know of any loan package to Thailand from commercial banks in Singapore.
The Development Bank of Singapore (DBS) said on Wednesday it was in touch with Thailand on the possibility of offering emergency credit lines.
"We are in touch with officials there. If there is a need, we will look at it in the most positive manner," DBS president Ng Kee Choe told Reuters. He declined to give further details.
Spokesmen for Singapore's remaining Big Four banks, OCBC Bank, United Overseas Bank and Overseas Union Bank, were either unavailable or declined to comment on possible aid to Thailand.
